record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.original_question: What practical methods can model changes to the rules by which a system’s structure evolves, including higher-order evolutionary changes such as changes to the rules that generate structural change, so that biological and social-system transformations can be modeled hierarchically?

evidence.quote:
we still have no practical approaches to modelling changes to the rules by which the system structure
evolves, much less ways to model even higher level changes.

As already mentioned we currently
have no way of modelling higher order evolutionary changes, like changes to the rules that generate
structural change in the system. Without such hierarchical evolutionary modelling techniques it will be
impossible to model the transformations that characterise social systems.

artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns developing practical hierarchical modeling frameworks for higher-order evolutionary change (rules changing, and rules-for-changing-rules changing). While related research exists (open-ended evolution, meta-dynamics, compositional/category-theoretic models of biology, e.g., Kauffman's adjacent possible, Andersen-Rasmussen-Sayama meta-dynamics), no widely accepted general practical framework has been established. The problem is broadly regarded as open in the theoretical biology and complex-systems communities.

status_evidence.title: Open-ended evolution and open-endedness
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the lack of formal frameworks for modeling open-ended, hierarchical evolutionary change in biological and artificial systems.
status_evidence.claim: Hierarchical modeling of changing evolutionary rules remains an open challenge in artificial life and theoretical biology.
